run.question: The payment-api pod in namespace app-101 had issues on November 20, 2026 around 13:45 UTC. What happened?

report.summary: The only direct evidence about the app-101 payment-api workload is its own log stream (Loki, job/service payment-api, file /var/log/payment-api.log, pod label payment-api-101-8486559b69-tj2ln). In that stream the last pre-incident record is a success at 13:42:00Z, and from 13:46:00Z the pod begins logging "Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted" with wait_time_ms and queue_length fields; eight such ERROR records appear between 13:46:00Z and 14:44:00Z. Successful "Payment processed successfully" records still occur during the interval (13:59:00Z, then 14:49:00Z and later), so this reads as intermittent degradation of the payment-api's database connection acquisition, not a total stop. The last pool-exhaustion record is at 14:44:00Z and no error records appear afterwards. The dependency itself is not observable: no database pod, service, statefulset or PVC exists anywhere in the cluster, so whether the exhaustion came from the database side or from the application's pool configuration remains unverified. Prometheus and Jaeger were unreachable (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE) for every attempt in this Run, so error-rate, latency, transaction-count and trace evidence for 13:45Z could not be read, and no Kubernetes event covers the incident time. Conclusion is partial: the symptom and its timing are well evidenced, the origin is not.

claims.text: The app-101 workload's log stream (labels service=payment-api, job=payment-api, namespace=app-101, pod=payment-api-101-8486559b69-tj2ln, filename=/var/log/payment-api.log) contains eight ERROR records with message "Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted" between 2026-11-20T13:46:00Z and 2026-11-20T14:44:00Z.

Before the incident the sampled window 2026-11-20T04:55:16Z-13:45:00Z contains 11 payment-api records, all level INFO "Payment processed successfully"; the last of them is at 2026-11-20T13:42:00Z (payment_id PAY-5032), and the first ERROR record follows at 13:46:00Z.

The pool-exhaustion records report increasing wait times and queue lengths: 13:46:00Z wait_time_ms 1227 queue_length 10; 13:54:00Z wait_time_ms 2104 queue_length 11; 14:03:00Z wait_time_ms 1495 queue_length 8; 14:15:00Z wait_time_ms 2965 queue_length 9; 14:19:00Z wait_time_ms 4005 queue_length 10; 14:21:00Z wait_time_ms 4840 queue_length 8; 14:31:00Z wait_time_ms 2358 queue_length 15; 14:44:00Z wait_time_ms 3836 queue_length 5.

Successful payments continue during the error interval: "Payment processed successfully" at 2026-11-20T13:59:00Z (PAY-1800) and again at 14:49:00Z (PAY-8206), 15:27:00Z and later, so the pod kept serving while database connection acquisition failed intermittently.

After the 14:44:00Z error the payment-api log stream contains only INFO records (successful payments) up to a final "Payment API started" record timestamped 2026-11-21T04:53:46.921141Z; no further ERROR record is present in the 14:30:00Z-2026-11-21T04:55:16Z window.

No database workload is visible in the cluster: the pod list cluster-wide contains no database pod, the service list contains no database service (payment-api itself has no Service), and the only StatefulSet is otel-demo/alertmanager; therefore the database that the log message refers to is not an observable cluster object.

Only one Loki stream set exists for the incident interval: in 13:40:00Z-13:50:00Z the query over all job label values returned only payment-api lines (13:42:00Z INFO success, 13:46:00Z ERROR pool exhausted), and aggregation by job/level over 12:30:00Z-14:30:00Z returned only job=payment-api series, so no other service's logs are available to attribute or corroborate the fault.

In the present cluster state namespace app-101 contains only the loki pod/replicaset/deployment (loki-66445c6d6f-9h7fr, image grafana/loki:2.9.0); no payment-api deployment, replicaset or pod exists now, and no pod named exactly "payment-api" is returned, while the name appearing in the log labels is payment-api-101-8486559b69-tj2ln.

The only app-101 events in the window are from 2026-11-21T04:53:22Z-04:53:59Z and are Normal reasons only: Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started for loki-66445c6d6f-9h7fr, then Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started/Killing for payment-api-101-8486559b69-tj2ln, plus ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate and Deployment ScalingReplicaSet (payment-api-101 scaled 0->1 at 04:53:45Z, loki 0->1); no event has a timestamp in the 2026-11-20T13:45Z period.

Namespace app-101 has creationTimestamp 2026-11-21T04:53:22Z, i.e. it was created after the reported 2026-11-20T13:45Z incident time, so the Nov 20 log records were ingested/attached to objects created later and cannot be corroborated by any surviving cluster object from the incident period.

app-101 holds only three ConfigMaps (kube-root-ca.crt, loki-config, promtail-config); there is no payment-api ConfigMap and no fault/delay/failure-injection setting for payment-api to read, and promtail-config shows the payment-api job is a static scrape of /var/log/*.log labelled job=payment-api, namespace=app-101.

The workload was not down: successful payment records exist at 13:42:00Z (before the first error), 13:59:00Z (inside the error interval) and 14:49:00Z (after the last 14:44 error), and the pre-incident sample 04:55:16Z-13:45:00Z shows no ERROR record at all, so an outage or a continuously failing service is not supported.

Within the app-101 event stream that is available (2026-11-21T04:53:22Z-04:53:59Z only) no Evicted, OOMKilled, BackOff or Unhealthy reason appears for the payment-api pod; the pod creation and deletion there are a controller rollout (ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate plus Deployment ScalingReplicaSet from 0 to 1), not evidence of the Nov 20 fault.

The pool exhaustion most likely originated in the database side (external dependency) - slow or saturated database causing connections to be held long enough to drain the pool - because the application self-reports 'pool exhausted' with rising wait_time_ms (1227 -> 4840) while it keeps completing some payments; this cannot be confirmed here because no database pod, service, statefulset or PVC exists in the cluster and no DB-side logs are in Loki.

An application-side connection-pool configuration or connection-leak problem in the payment-api container (pool size/timeout too small, connections not returned) is an alternative explanation for the same log signature; it cannot be evaluated because the payment-api Deployment and pod no longer exist, so container env, resource limits and pool settings are unknown, and app-101 has no payment-api ConfigMap.

A traffic increase or a configuration change around 13:45Z could have triggered the exhaustion, but nothing in this Run supports it: the Prometheus-backed tools (app_payment_transactions_total, traces_span_metrics_calls_total, http_server_request_duration_seconds_count, kube_deployment_status_*) were unreachable, no Kubernetes event carries a 2026-11-20 timestamp, and no change-history source is integrated.

Obtain evidence from the database the payment-api uses (outside this cluster): its connection limits, active/max connections, latency and slow queries for 2026-11-20T13:40Z-14:50Z, since the cluster contains no database workload to inspect.

Recover the payment-api Deployment manifest (pool size, acquire timeout, leak detection, resource limits) and compare it with any change made before 13:45Z, since the current cluster holds no payment-api Deployment or ConfigMap to compare against.

Restore read access to Prometheus and Jaeger for the incident window so error rate, transaction counts, latency distribution and trace status for payment-api around 13:45Z can be quantified instead of inferred from eight log lines.

gaps: All Prometheus-backed tools (execute_prometheus_instant_query, metrics_range_query, get_series, get_label_values, get_metric_names, list_prometheus_rules, get_prometheus_target) failed with SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE in this Run, so app_payment_transactions_total, traces_span_metrics_calls_total, http_server_request_duration_seconds_count, rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count, rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket and kube_deployment_status_replicas_* were never read for 2026-11-20T13:45Z; no metric-based error rate, throughput or latency baseline exists in this report.

All Jaeger tools (traces_list_services, traces_list_operations, traces_search, traces_search_by_tags) failed with SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no span, status-code or duration evidence for service payment or the app-101 payment-api was obtained.

No database dependency of payment-api is visible: no database pod, service, statefulset, PVC or log stream exists in the cluster, so the database identity, its health and whether the exhaustion originated there are unknown.

No Kubernetes event covers 2026-11-20T13:45Z: the available event stream spans 2026-11-21T04:23:43Z-04:53:59Z, so whether anything changed (rollout, config change, restart) at the incident time cannot be confirmed.
change_history is not an integrated source in this Run, so no record of a configuration or deployment change before 13:45Z could be checked.

The payment-api Deployment, ReplicaSet and pod no longer exist and namespace app-101 was created at 2026-11-21T04:53:22Z, so pod status, container last-termination reason/exit code, restart count and pod events for the incident period are unknown; the Nov 20 log records were ingested after these objects were created, leaving the provenance of their timestamps unverified.

An exact entity named "payment-api" (pod) returned nothing: the pods query for namespace app-101 returned only loki-66445c6d6f-9h7fr, and no pod named payment-api exists cluster-wide; the related but differently named entity observed in the logs is pod payment-api-101-8486559b69-tj2ln (namespace app-101, service/job label payment-api).

Only eight ERROR records and a sparse set of INFO records exist for payment-api, so no error-rate or denominator is available and the complete request history of the pod during 13:45Z-14:45Z is unknown.

data.loki-config.yaml:
auth_enabled: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
server:
  http_listen_port: 3100
ingester:
  query_store_max_look_back_period: -1
  max_chunk_age: 17520h  # 2 years
  wal:
    enabled: false
  lifecycler:
    address: 127.0.0.1
    ring:
      kvstore:
        store: inmemory
      replication_factor: 1
    final_sleep: 0s
chunk_store_config:
  max_look_back_period: 17520h  # 2 years
schema_config:
  configs:
    - from: 2020-01-01
      store: boltdb
      object_store: filesystem
      schema: v11
      index:
        prefix: index_
        period: 168h
storage_config:
  boltdb:
    directory: /tmp/loki/index
  filesystem:
    directory: /tmp/loki/chunks
limits_config:
  enforce_metric_name: false
  reject_old_samples: false
  reject_old_samples_max_age: 104w  # 2 years
  max_entries_limit_per_query: 5000
  max_query_lookback: 17520h  # 2 years

data.promtail-config.yaml:
server:
  http_listen_port: 9080
positions:
  filename: /tmp/positions.yaml
  sync_period: 10s
  ignore_invalid_yaml: true
clients:
  - url: http://loki:3100/loki/api/v1/push
    batchwait: 100ms       # Send batches more frequently
    batchsize: 102400      # 100KB batch size (smaller batches)
    backoff_config:
      min_period: 100ms
      max_period: 1m
      max_retries: 20
    timeout: 10s
scrape_configs:
  - job_name: payment-api
    static_configs:
      - targets:
          - localhost
        labels:
          job: payment-api
          namespace: app-101
          __path__: /var/log/*.log
    pipeline_stages:
      - json:
          expressions:
            timestamp: timestamp
            level: level
            message: message
            service: service
            pod: pod
      - timestamp:
          source: timestamp
          format: RFC3339
      - labels:
          level:
          service:
          pod:
